stops.imageCaption: Sun-warmed volcanic-stone Mexican Baroque cloister and bustling sunlit courtyard framed by blue-tiled domes beneath bright highland skies.

stops.title: Planting the First Bell at Mission San Diego de Alcalá
stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across Mission San Diego de Alcalá to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.imageCaption: Crisp whitewashed Spanish colonial adobe bell wall silhouetted against brilliant Pacific blue skies and sunlit golden coastal hills.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Mission San Diego de Alcalá’s iconic five-bell whitewashed adobe campanario still stands as a lively parish and California’s oldest historic mission site.
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: When frightened expedition leaders nearly voted to abandon starving San Diego and sail back to Mexico in 1770, stubborn Father Serra refused to board the ship—praying a nine-day novena to St. Joseph until the rescue supply ship *San Antonio* literally sailed over the horizon on St. Joseph’s Day, March 19!
stops.saintQuote: To speak of going back is out of the question—always forward!

hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: Limping overland from Baja California through scorching deserts with his swollen leg, fifty-five-year-old Father Serra reached San Diego Bay in July 1769, hung a bronze bell from a leafy oak tree, and founded **Mission San Diego de Alcalá**—the first link in California’s iconic 600-mile **El Camino Real**! Over the next fifteen years, walking thousands of coastal miles despite asthma and constant pain, he personally founded **nine** missions that birthed modern San Diego, Carmel, San Luis Obispo, San Francisco, and Santa Clara.

stops.title: Home by the Cypress Sea at Carmel Mission
stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across Mission San Carlos Borromeo de Carmelo to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.ancientPlaceName: Mission San Carlos Borromeo de Carmelo
stops.imageCaption: Warm golden sandstone Moorish-domed mission basilica framed by blooming bougainvillea and gnarled cypresses overlooking the sparkling misty Pacific Ocean.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Carmel Mission Basilica—widely called the jewel of California’s missions—welcomes visitors to pray beside St. Junípero Serra’s stone sanctuary tomb and step inside his preserved tiny adobe bedroom.
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: When Pope Francis canonized St. Junípero Serra in September 2015, he celebrated him as an tireless missionary who kept going forward with joy—and California’s golden sandstone Carmel Mission still rings his original bells!
stops.saintQuote: I promise you I will not forget you when I reach heaven.

hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: Falling in love with the misty cypress coast and sparkling bay of Carmel, St. Junípero Serra made **Mission San Carlos Borromeo de Carmelo** his home headquarters for his final fourteen years—living in a tiny bare-walled adobe cell with a wooden plank bed and a small desk where he wrote hundreds of letters. Passing away peacefully on August 28, 1784 at age seventy, he was canonized right in Washington, D.C. in 2015—the first saint ever canonized on United States soil!

globeHeaderSubtitle: Sacred Trails of St. Otto of Bamberg (Bamberg (Germany) & Szczecin (Poland))
completionSummary: You journeyed from Franconia’s four-spired imperial cathedral all the way to the breezy Baltic coast with St. Otto of Bamberg—the "Apostle of Pomerania" who healed imperial feuds as a peacemaker and won northern Europe by bringing gifts, fairness, and respect instead of swords.

stops.title: Peacemaker-Bishop of Four-Spired Bamberg
stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across Babenberga (Bamberg Cathedral) to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.imageCaption: Majestic four-spired pale sandstone Romanesque imperial cathedral glowing in golden Franconian light above historic timbered river houses.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Bamberg’s breathtaking UNESCO Old Town and four-spired Cathedral still glow with the architectural and charitable vision St. Otto poured into Franconia.
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: During a devastating Bavarian famine, Bishop Otto refused to dine on fine food—spending the entire episcopal treasury to buy grain and personally distributing loaves so thousands of families survived!
stops.saintQuote: True authority is measured by how gently it lifts the poor.

hiddenArtifacts.foundTitle: Peacemaker-Bishop of Four-Spired Bamberg
hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: Born into a modest Swabian noble family around 1060, gifted young Otto spent years teaching in Poland—learning Slavic languages fluently!—before becoming imperial chancellor and Bishop of Bamberg in 1102. Entering Bamberg barefoot in winter snow to show his humility, Otto rebuilt Bamberg Cathedral after a fire, founded over twenty monasteries and free hospitals, and acted as the brilliant bridge-building diplomat who helped end the bitter 50-year Investiture Controversy with the **Concordat of Worms** in 1122!

stops.title: Breezy Baltic Voyage to Szczecin & Pomerania
stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across Stettin (Szczecin, Pomerania) to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.imageCaption: Breezy amber-lit Baltic port harbor framed by timber medieval ships and tall coastal pines as a tall smiling bishop hands gifts to curious Pomeranian townspeople.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Across northern Poland and northeastern Germany, St. Otto of Bamberg is cherished as the beloved **"Apostle of Pomerania"**—celebrated for proving that genuine friendship achieves what armies never could!
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: Otto deliberately arrived in Pomerania dressed cleanly and generously paying his own way—because earlier beggared missionaries had been mocked as fortune-hunters! His thoughtful cultural sensitivity won entire cities overnight!
stops.saintQuote: We have not come to take your silver, but to share a treasure that can never be stolen.

hiddenArtifacts.foundTitle: Breezy Baltic Voyage to Szczecin & Pomerania
hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: When Polish Duke Bolesław III begged someone to preach the Gospel to the fiercely independent Baltic Pomeranians—where earlier harsh preachers had failed completely!—sixty-four-year-old Bishop Otto stepped forward with a genius strategy: **never ask for a single coin, and come bringing generous gifts, fair trade, and total respect!** Speaking fluent Slavic, redeeming captives from slavery, and arriving with wagonloads of fine cloth and provisions for the poor, Otto peacefully baptized over 22,000 Pomeranians across Szczecin, Wolin, and Pyrzyce!

detectiveClues.clueText: Returning home to Bamberg after two legendary Baltic missionary journeys, elderly Bishop Otto kept founding hospitals, restoring churches, and writing letters of encouragement to his newborn Pomeranian parishes right until his peaceful passing on June 30, 1139. Canonized fifty years later, he rests inside his beloved hilltop Abbey of St. Michael overlooking the valley he loved.
